title: Chapter 10. The Journey to Vrindavana
html:
Virachandra dismisses his companions and travels through Jharikhanda to Vrindavana; the Madanamohana temple and the story of Abhirama-Sridama; Gaya, Kashi and the tale of Shiva and Bhuvaneshvara; meeting with Jiva Gosvami, arati and kirtana in Vrindavana; a vision of the rasa; Radhakunda and Govardhana; the author's conclusion (pp. 78–91)

[p. 78]

1Glory, glory to merciful Sri Krishna Chaitanya!
Glory to Nityananda, glory, glory to Virachandra!

2Brothers, sing the qualities of Nitai and Chaitanya!
Sing just once, and see how soothed you become.

On this, a song:1

3Hari, Hari! Will I ever have such a birth again?
I, so unfortunate — will I see again with my own eyes
Gaura's descent in Nadia?

4The hidden treasure of Goloka — the sankirtana of Hari-nama —
he revealed in every home.
Except for me, wretched one, all the people of the world received it,
and the whole world became rich.

5Says Vrindavana Dasa: my one constant desire
is to sing the qualities of Nitai and Chaitanya.
May the names of Nitai and Chaitanya shine ceaselessly in my heart —
apart from this I want nothing.

6Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya, glory to the abode of rasa!
Glory to Nityananda, glory to the name of Virachandra!

7Having filled the land of Rarh2 with the bliss of prema,
Prabhu was seized by the longing: "I will go to Vrindavana."

8All the dear devotees who were with Prabhu
he sent off, saying: "Go to Khardaha."

9Ramai, Sundarananda3 and other close ones
received Prabhu's order and set off.

10Five or seven people remained with Prabhu;
they said: "We will go along with Prabhu."

11Prabhu said: "All of you, heed my word:
go home and always chant the name of Krishna."

[p. 79]

12Prabhu intended to go by the road through Jharikhanda4.
At dawn the sankirtana of Hari-nama arose.

13Who can say what the Self-willed One will do?
He stopped at the gate of a certain temple.

14The place was charming and full of fragrance;
as soon as the scent entered his nostrils, Prabhu was filled with prema.

15He ran inside the temple compound,
looked here and there, and became almost mad.

16The temple pujari, all in a bustle,
opened the doors so that he could have darshan.

17Seeing the Deity, Prabhu lost his composure:
his whole body bristled with ecstasy, tears flowed from his eyes.

18Prabhu asked under what name the Deity resided there.
"Sri Madanamohana," the man replied.

19The moment he heard this, Prabhu's prema welled up.
United with Radha's body, [Krishna] became golden in color —

20this Gaura descended in Navadvipa:
concealing his own complexion, he accepted [her] luster.

21Within he is full of rasa, with Krishna's luster;
without, the luster of the beloved is seen, radiant.

22For this reason Gauranga is called the King of rasa:
Rasavati5 covers him from above.

23Thus Radha and Krishna are Gaura, the Bhagavan;
Radha and Krishna are one soul, so the Vedas declare.

24With great difficulty he restrained that emotion
and gazed unblinkingly at Srimati6.

25Prabhu said: "In Vrindavana he is gracefully bent in three places;
why is he bent even more here?"

26The pujari replied: "He was gracefully bent in three places,
but at Abhirama's obeisance he became bent even more."7

27Hearing this, Prabhu told him:
"Krishna knows how to magnify his devotee's glory."

28Of the supreme greatness of Abhirama Gopala
he told everyone, explaining the truth of it.

29When Prabhu8 was wandering as an avadhuta,
he came in longing to the land of Vrindavana.

30Not seeing Krishna, he pined intensely
and called out loudly: "Brother Sridama!"

31Out of Govardhana Hill [Sridama] emerged
and, sounding his horn and flute, came to meet him.

32His luster bright as gold, dressed like a dancer,
in yellow cloth, a staff in hand, absorbed in love of Krishna.

33He asked Prabhu: "What great person are you?
Why have you called me?

34I cannot recognize you: your color has changed.
I thought my elder brother Balarama was calling me.

35Hearing that voice, I came.
Tell me for certain: who are you?"

36When brother Sridama asked this,
Balarama made himself known.

37Sridama said: "Where are your horn, your cowherd dress and crown?
You have given up your elegance and become shaven-headed!

38If only I could see the enchanting flute in Kanai's9 hand,
at whose sound all the cows would gather!

39The cows would wander to distant forests, lured by grass,
and he would call them, herd by herd, with the sound of his flute.

40Why have you hidden your white-fair complexion and become reddish-gold?
I cannot believe you are 'brother Balarama.'

41Come, I'll clap your hand
and run away all the way to the Yamuna.

42If you can catch me, then I'll know you are Bali10."
Saying this, he clapped his hand.

[p. 80]

43Crying "Run!", he fled down the road,
but within ten steps [Balarama] caught him.

44Saying "Brother!", he touched his ear with his hand
and assumed his white, fair form, holding plough and club.

45He said: "Now the age of Kali has come,
and you are still asleep, you foolish cowherd folk!"

46Placing the plough on his shoulder, he pulled
and spoke these words: "Grow big!"11

47Then he grew to four cubits of his own hand —
a beautiful body, a mahapurusha in person.

48That pure mood of friendship (sakhya) abides in him always;
therefore his name became "Abhirama Gopala."

49Laughing, Sridama said: "Listen, brother,
where is Kanai, dearer to you than life?

50You could not stay apart from him even once —
how and why have you left that Krishna?

51We know: you are two brothers but one soul.
How is it that you wander alone without him?"

52Rama laughed and said: "He has gone to the land of Gauda
and descended [there] together with all the cowherd boys and girls.

53In a village named Navadvipa, on the bank of the Jahnavi12,
he delivered living beings by performing the sacrifice of sankirtana."

54All these stories Virachandra told,
and the Vaishnavas, hearing them, were filled with joy.

55Prabhu said: "I heard this from Uddharana Datta13:
he was with Prabhu during his pilgrimage to the holy places."

56All the Vaishnavas cried: "Hari, Hari!"
Hearing this, Prabhu Virachandra rejoiced at heart.

57Having circumambulated the temple, Gosai
went and stayed at the house of some fortunate man.

58At dawn Prabhu set out through Jharikhanda,
making Vaishnavas of all kinds of people.

59Thieves, bandits, highway robbers and cutthroats —
by Prabhu's mercy every one of them became a devotee.

60Giving up violence and hatred, all chant the name of Krishna —
such is what the mercy of a Prabhu like Virachandra brings about.

61There has not been and will not be such an avatara
as Gaurachandra, Nityananda and Virachandra.

62So mercifully did Prabhu look upon Jharikhanda
that [there] no one ever worships other gods.

63Crying "Radha-Krishna, Nityananda, Vira, Chaitanya!",
all perform sankirtana, intoxicated with prema.

64Earlier, Gaurachandra, going to the land of Vrindavana,
delivered many by the same route14.

65Calling "Krishna, Krishna!" as he walked along the road,
he passed through many lands, lost in prema.

66Virachandra Mahaprabhu, showing mercy to living beings,
went on step by step, delivering everyone.

67The road went through dense forest, laden with fruit and flowers;
drunk on honey, countless bees were humming.

68How many cuckoos and peacocks sang and danced!
On the soft, soft breeze the flower pollen drifted down.

69Stags and does, gathered in herds,
roamed about, absorbed in play.

70Bull elephants roamed together with cow elephants;
the mountain peaks were exceedingly beautiful.

71Thus the beasts and birds sported in the forest,
and alongside them tigers, bears and rhinoceroses.

72Seeing this, how delighted Prabhu Virachandra was!
"Come, come!" he called to them all.

73Prabhu said: "All together, say 'Krishna, Krishna!'"
Hearing Prabhu's words, [the animals] were overwhelmed with prema.

[p. 81]

74Hearing Prabhu's word and gazing at his face,
all of them cried "Krishna, Krishna!" at the top of their voices.

75The animals did no harm to one another;
all said "Krishna, Krishna" with joyful hearts.

76Sitting in the trees, the birds sweetly sang:
"Krishna, Krishna, Hari, Hari, Govinda, Gopala!"

77Hearing this, Prabhu Virachandra rejoiced at heart —
this is how he attracted the beasts and birds.

78In everyone's heart Virachandra dwells:
whatever he makes them say, to that the mind inclines.

79Hearing the name of Krishna from the mouths of beasts and birds,
Prabhu Virachandra was immersed in the happiness of love for Krishna.

80As once, when Radha and Krishna sported in Vrindavana,
the beasts and birds looked on,

81[so now] they chanted the names of Radha and Krishna, full of prema;
in that mood Virachandra lost all self-control.

82Meditating in his heart on the pastimes of Radha and Krishna
and seeing the beauty of the forest, Prabhu floated in bliss.

83Thus Prabhu performed his secret pastimes in the forest;
seeing the beauty of the forest, Prabhu rejoiced at heart.

84The Vaishnavas with him, seeing this wonder,
all considered these pastimes of Prabhu astonishing.

85He entered terrible, dense forests,
and seeing them, Prabhu felt great joy.

86"This is Vrindavana!" he said, floating in prema,
and wept, crying: "Ha, ha, Vrindavanachandra!"

87Prabhu said: "The happiness I have found in this forest —
not a drop of it exists in the world of Vaikuntha."

88Thus, step by step, he came to Gaya.
Seeing the "Vishnupada"15, he said: "My eyes are soothed!"

89All the associates who dwell in Vishnu's abode [are present here];
this place equals Vaikuntha, its riches are incomparable.

90For three days he rested in that place
and saw all the sites of Vishnu's pastimes.

91With great care Prabhu fed the brahmanas
and gave them many jewels in abundance.

92Continuing on his way, he came to Kashi16
and, saying "This is the place of liberation," looked upon Vishveshvara.

93After resting, he bathed and took refreshment17
and told everyone the tale of Mahesha.

94"Once Shankara dwelt in this abode of Kashi.
Pleased with the king of Kashi, he granted him a boon.

95[The king] asked for the boon of conquering Vishnu,
and the carefree Bholanatha18 said: 'So be it.'

96Intoxicated by the boon, deluded, the wretched [king] went to Dvaraka
and gave battle to Krishna.

97Defeated in battle, he came back to Shiva
and, coming, told him everything in detail.

98Hearing this, Rudra became like the fire of universal dissolution;
under the influence of tamo-guna his understanding of the Bhagavan was dimmed.

99Kartika, Ganesha, ghosts, spirits, yakshas and demons —
[taking them] as an army, he mounted the bull and took up the trident.

100Sending the king of Kashi ahead with a great army,
he went again and besieged the city of Dvaraka.

101Hearing this, the Lord of the Yadus, filled with anger,
came out holding the disc.

102Having playfully cut off the head of the king of Kashi,
the disc came back and stood near him, [as if] with joined palms.

103Shankara in his pride, not recognizing the Lord,
angrily released the pashupata weapon.

104Seeing Shiva's pride, [Krishna] smiled slightly
and gave this order to the Sudarshana disc:

[p. 82]

105'Repel the pashupata, [go] to Kashi
and burn it to ashes with your own heat.

106Having terrified Shiva, go after him
and today throw him into utter disarray.'

107'As you command!' — and the disc rushed off at great speed;
frightened, Rudra fled in confusion.

108[The disc] burned Kashi to ashes.
In fear of the disc, Shiva wandered through all three worlds.

109Shiva said: 'Who will shelter me from this disc?
There is no one to stop it except Krishna alone.'

110He appeared again in Dvaraka,
and as soon as he entered [that] abode, his tamo-guna left him.

111Coming, he fell at Krishna's lotus feet;
seeing Shiva, Krishna smiled slightly.

112Overcome with prema, Mahadeva offers praise:
'You gave me tamo-guna and made me almost mad.

113By your appointment I perform all my deeds,
but I myself do not know what is dharma and what is not dharma for me.

114I want nothing more to do with such misdeeds;
my trident I will henceforth keep to myself, Gosai19.

115I have no use for tamo-guna; I will take pure sattva-guna
and, free of selfish desires, serve your feet.'

116Saying this, he threw himself [on the ground] before him;
Krishna took him by the hand and lifted him up.

117Graciously he began to speak to him:
'Bholanatha, never again be so forgetful (bhola).'20

118Shiva said: 'You have burned my abode —
now I will live in your own abode.'

119Krishna said: 'Of all my eternal abodes,
listen, Shiva, I have given you one place.

120Ekamra-kanana is a charming forest region;
there you will be the Lord of millions of lingas21.

121It is a beautiful city like Varanasi,
and next to it is my supremely secret abode.

122I, Shiva, will tell you about this place;
no one knows the secret of that abode.

123On the shore of the ocean, at the root of the banyan, is the abode of Nilachala,
Kshetra Purushottama22, a most delightful place.

124When time destroys the countless universes,
even then it can do nothing to that place.

125I always dwell in that place,
and every day my meal is served there.

126By the power of that place, over ten yojanas23 of land,
all the living beings — creatures, insects and worms that dwell there —

127all appear four-armed to the gods;
there, it is said, death is a blessing.

128Sleep in that place brings the fruit of samadhi;
lying down there equals an obeisance, as the Vedas say.

129Walking about there one gets the fruit of circumambulation,
and mere talk there is like a hymn to me.

130So great and pure is the power of that holy place
that even one who eats fish gets the fruit of havishya24.

131This place that bears my own name is so dear to me;
all who live there are equal to me.

132There the staff of Yama has no authority:
I myself judge the good and bad of all.

133To the north of this abode of mine
I have given you a place to live.

134It is a charming place, bestowing both enjoyment and liberation;
there you will be famed as Sri Bhuvaneshvara.

135Now Bhuvaneshvara is a manifestation of Kashi;
taking many forms, dwell there.'

[p. 83]

136Hearing of the glory of that abode, Shankara
again clasped the holy feet and replied:

137'Listen, lord of my life, to one request of mine:
I am always full of the greatest pride.

138If I, leaving you, live in another place,
there will be no well-being for me for a single moment.

139My mind wishes to stay near you;
[otherwise], through the fault of bad company, I may one day fall away [from you].

140If you regard me as your servant at all,
then give me a place in your own holy abode.

141Hearing from your holy lips of the glory of that place,
I have conceived a great desire to live there.

142I will serve you, Lord, as the lowest of all;
give me a place there, Lord, even the size of a sesame seed.

143My mind is strongly drawn to living in that holy abode.'
Saying this, Maheshvara wept.

144Shiva's words pleased the Moon-faced One,
and, embracing him, [Krishna] began to speak:

145'Listen, Shiva: you are like my own body to me;
whoever is dear to you is dearest of all to me.

146Where you are, there I am; in this there is no difference.
In all [my] holy places I have given you a place.

147You are the guardian of all my holy places everywhere;
in all holy places I have given you authority.

148I have given you Ekamra-kanana —
dwell there too in your full form.

149That place is supremely dear to me;
out of love for me you will live there always.

150Whoever, calling himself my devotee, does not honor you
merely mocks me.'

151Hearing this, Shiva was delighted
and took up his residence in Bhuvaneshvara."

152Hearing this, the Vaishnavas rejoiced at heart
and told everyone of the inconceivable pastimes of the Lord.

153Then [Prabhu] came to Prayaga25;
seeing Venimadhava, his heart was filled with prema.

154He stayed there three days in kirtana and dancing;
seeing this, the people of Prayaga marveled at heart.

155Thus he entered Vrindavana;
the moment he saw it, he was seized by prema.

156[Seeing] Vrindavana of eighty-four kroshas26, the living land,
he prostrated himself fully and began to offer praise:

157"Glory, glory to Vrindavana, to all that is moving and unmoving!
All are dear to Krishna, all are like Krishna's own body.

158Glory to Vrinda Devi27, boundless is your greatness!
By your mercy may Krishna accept me.

159Glory to Vrinda Devi, I bow at your feet:
make me a handmaid of Radha and Ananga28.

160Glory to Krishna, Baladeva, Vrindavanachandra!
Make me your own and cut the bonds of worldly existence."

161Having prayed thus, Virachandra
went on, repeating again and again: "Ha, Krishna, Govinda!"

162Prabhu is the instructing guru who teaches all people:
by practicing bhakti himself he makes it known to the world.

163Hearing that Prabhu had come to Vraja, the Vaishnavas
came out ahead to meet him and see him.

164In the temple a joyful clamor arose;
Gaudeshvara Gosai29 too came to that place.

165The Vaishnavas of Gauda came along performing kirtana;
at the sight of Prabhu a festival swelled in their hearts.

166Seeing Prabhu's beauty, the Vaishnavas
all said: "This is the son of Shachi himself!"

[p. 84]

167The Vaishnavas fell down flat like sticks;
Prabhu raised each one, placing his hand on his head.

168Prabhu said: "Everyone, perform the sankirtana of Krishna's name!" —
and all the Vaishnavas began to sing.

169Prabhu went on foot to the temple gate;
the fragrance of Krishna's body reached his nostrils.

170Reeling [in prema], he fell on that spot,
and the Vaishnavas, surrounding him, sang kirtana.

171After a long while he restrained that mood
and went to have darshan of Govinda.

172Unblinking, he gazed at [his] two feet
and, beholding them, became immersed in the bliss of his own mood.

173Having viewed Govinda from feet to head,
he fixed his eyes on the orb of his holy face.

174Then, seeing Madanamohana again,
he stood as if stunned, his gaze fixed on his chest.

175Seeing Sri Jahnava30 at the left side,
Prabhu, almost fainting, swayed and fell.

176His eyes rolled upward, his breath came fast and fast;
now his body seemed to grow thin, now he flung his limbs about.

177Thus in that mood [time passed] until the third watch31;
in hundreds upon hundreds of ways his emotion moved.

178Then the devotees, surrounding Prabhu,
loudly sang the sankirtana of the holy name.

179"Sri Jahnava! Gopinatha!" he cried aloud.
After some time Hari32 returned to outward consciousness:

180"Ha, ha, Jahnava! Gopinatha, lord of my life!
Cast a merciful glance: I am a low sinner."

181Composing himself, Prabhu met with the Vaishnavas;
coming out of the temple, they all sat down.

182Sanatana's nephew, whose name was Sri Jiva,
with joined palms fell flat in obeisance.

183Prabhu asked: "Who is this noble person?"
The chief one, Haridasa33, told him all about him.

184Hearing this, Prabhu was delighted and showed him great mercy;
he began to speak of the virtues of Rupa and Sanatana:

185"This is the incomparable achievement of Rupa and Sanatana —
that through the rasa of bhakti [these] holy forms became manifest.

186I have heard that you are a great and profound pandita;
please my heart too by letting me hear [you]."

187Jiva said: "All this is the grace of your feet;
you make a mute man a eulogist — there is no error in that."

On this it is said:

188"Him by whose mercy the mute become eloquent and the lame cross mountains —
him I worship, Paramananda the Lord."34

189"By whose will the ocean becomes dry land, dry land the ocean, a speck of dust a mountain,
a mountain earth, a blade of grass a thunderbolt, and a thunderbolt a blade of grass,
fire becomes coolness and snow burning heat —
to that Krishna who delights in wondrous, unrestrained pastimes, obeisance."35

[p. 85]

190Thus Jiva Gosai, before Prabhu,
lovingly expounded [the teaching of] devotion to Krishna.

191Hearing this, Virachandra was very pleased
and, overflowing with prema, embraced Jiva:

192"You have certainly received Chaitanya's mercy:
without Chaitanya's mercy there is no such revelation.

193Prabhu showed great kindness to your family:
I have heard that formerly they saw Him in person."

194Jiva said: "You are Chaitanya himself,
come here to show me mercy.

195Who has the power to understand your pastimes?
You have manifested your pastimes again to preserve bhakti.

196This is a hidden avatara for the deliverance of living beings;
even Brahma, Shiva and the rest cannot know it.

197When and what you do, even the Vedas do not know;
how can the Vedas know the independent Lord?

198Inconceivable are your pastimes, inaccessible to the Vedas,
but easily accessible to the one to whom you reveal them.

199This avatara of yours is most secret:
the one to whom you reveal it knows it for certain."

200Thus, with Jiva, in the sweetness of talks about Krishna,
the two of them, in the rapture of prema, spoke of each other's greatness.

201Who can relate this conversation of master and servant?
Without bhakti no one can know Krishna.

202Thus there were many talks about Krishna;
fearing to lengthen the book, I have not related them in detail.

203Virachandra descended to distribute prema;
he taught Jiva36 the essence of the truth of prema-bhakti.

204This essence of prema-bhakti he told Jiva;
hearing it, Jiva Gosai was immersed in the sweetness of prema.

205Master and servant, embracing each other's necks,
both rolled on the ground, crying: "Ha, Krishna Chaitanya!"

206As formerly in Kashi the son of Shachi
taught Sanatana the truth of bhakti,

207so [Virachandra] told Jiva Gosai
about bhakti — the essence of siddhanta, the greatness of bhakti.

208Jiva received much mercy.
At that time the pujari Gosaidasa37 arrived.

209Coming, he fell flat at Prabhu's feet
and, with joined palms, began to speak before Prabhu:

210"Please come into the temple:
evening has come, the time of arati."

211Prabhu was delighted, exclaiming "Gauranga!",
and went and entered the temple.

212[The pujari], having prepared the five-wick lamp for arati,
knowingly placed it in Prabhu's hand.

213[Prabhu] performed arati as his heart prompted,
offering the conch with water, the fan38 and the rest.

214In the courtyard a joyful kirtana began;
hearing it, the people of Vraja went wild with ecstasy.

215Then the pujari took that same arati lamp
and performed arati to Prabhu himself.

216"What are you doing, what are you doing?" Prabhu said to the pujari.
The pujari replied: "No one has independent power.

217Whatever you, Prabhu, make a living being do, that he does;
without your will no one can do anything."

218Prabhu said: "You are all learned men;
it is not proper for you to treat a living being so."

219Saying this, Prabhu smiled a little
and, chanting the name of Krishna, bowed to the Thakura39.

220Prabhu went into the midst of the sankirtana;
how joyful the devotees were to see Prabhu!

[p. 86]

221In the midst of the sankirtana Prabhu began [to dance];
how joyful he was to hear the sound of Krishna's name!

222All sang kirtana at the top of their voices:
"Govinda, Gopala, Rama, Krishna, Hari, Hari!"

223Filled with prema, Prabhu, in the rapture of dance,
raised both arms and danced in the sweetness of love for Krishna.

224Dancing and dancing, Prabhu became frenzied;
under the weight of his steps the earth began to tremble.

225The devotees thought it was an earthquake;
the sound of the kirtana pervaded the three worlds.

226In the midst of the sankirtana Prabhu revealed his power:
all beheld the sankirtana pastime of Mahaprabhu.

227Crying "Krishna, Krishna!", Prabhu danced:
now he laughed, now he sighed heavily, now he wept.

228His body was covered with gooseflesh, his hair stood on end;
hearing his thunderous roar, everyone was afraid.

229Now sweat, now trembling, and at times it happened
that all saw his body two or three times larger.

230Now his body became very thin, now it was stunned motionless;
seeing this, all the people were amazed.

231Now they saw him as Shyamasundara, bent in three places,
playing the enchanting flute held to his lips;

232now white, with plough and club in his hands;
now they saw his body the color of molten gold,

233with staff and kamandalu in hand in the midst of the kirtana —
Chaitanya Gosai himself shone in the kirtana;

234now they saw a great radiance the color of dawn —
a form of millions of Kandarpas shone in the kirtana.

235Such moods arose as cannot be described:
one never knows in what mood Virachandra Raya is dancing.

236Seeing this, the people of Vraja were amazed:
"Never have we seen such a wondrous kirtana!"

237The temple people40, seeing this, marveled;
all said: "This is Chaitanya descended in person!

238We heard that Mahaprabhu in the town of Nadia,
the son of Shachi, performed the pastime of sankirtana.

239That we heard, and now we have seen it with our own eyes in Vrindavana:
here is Krishna Chaitanya himself in person.

240The same form, the same radiance, the same sankirtana,
the same mood, the same prema, the same signs, the same dance."

241How many surges of prema there were in Vrindavana!
In what mood he does what is hard to understand.

242Thus the kirtana went on for a long time,
and all the singers and players grew weary.

243Seeing this, Prabhu restrained his mood;
stopping the kirtana, all took rest.

244The pujari Gosaidasa and all the temple people
devotedly rendered Prabhu all kinds of service.

245Every day there was kirtana and dancing in every grove;
and sometimes he went alone wherever his heart led him.

246Sometimes he went around the town with kirtana,
sometimes to the solitary forest on the bank of the Yamuna.

247Sitting beneath Amli-tala41, he wept
and, crying "Ha, Krishna Chaitanya!", lost consciousness.

248Sometimes, coming to Shringara-vata42, he would sit
and weep, crying: "Ha, ha, Prabhu Nityananda!

249Where is my Prabhu, my life, Nitai-Balai?
Where is the lord of my life, Kanai, my very life?"

250Remembering Krishna's pastimes, Prabhu fell into such a state
that sometimes he lay [unconscious] until the second watch.

251The devotees loudly sang of Krishna's pastimes
and, when he regained consciousness, took him back to their lodging.

[p. 87]

252Sometimes at night Prabhu would wander
and, going to a solitary spot, gaze at the Yamuna.

253Sometimes, after having darshan of Gopeshvara43,
Prabhu would go and sit on the bank at Vamshivata.

254Seeing the beauty of the trees and creepers, he rejoiced at heart
and, sitting there, sang the sankirtana of the holy name:

255"Glory to Krishna, Baladeva, Rasika Murari!
Glory to Radha, Govinda, Gopala, Giridhari!

256Glory to Radha and Gopinatha, treasure of Jahnava's life44!
Glory, glory to Krishna, glory to Madanamohana!

257Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare,
Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare!"

258Thus Virachandra, at the top of his voice,
absorbed in prema, sang the garland of Govinda's names.

259Hearing the sound of the kirtana, the beasts and birds
surrounded Prabhu and all began to dance.

260Spreading their tails, peacocks and peahens dance;
the moonlit night shimmers, [the] waves of the Yamuna [play].

261Herd after herd the deer come, hearing the kirtana,
and with restless eyes gaze intently at Prabhu.

262Male and female cuckoos, raising their voices,
chant the name of Krishna together with Prabhu at the top of their voices.

263So too all the trees and creepers of Vrindavana,
intoxicated with prema, sing the names of Radha and Krishna.

264Thus Prabhu enjoyed the happiness of prema.
One day Prabhu went onto the river sandbank45.

265How delighted he was to see the beauty of the sandbank!
Seeing the forest served by Vrinda, he was happy.

266The moonlit night shimmers, a gentle breeze blows,
the nostrils are filled with the scent of fragrant flowers.

267The trees and creepers, with fruit and flowers, were most beautiful;
seeing them, Prabhu marveled at heart.

268The mood of Krishna's pastimes came and arose [in him];
crying "Ha, ha, Radha-Krishna!", Prabhu fainted.

269Possessed by the mood of the gopis, identified with it, [he sees]
Krishna performing the rasa with all the gopis.

270In the middle are Radha and Krishna, on all sides the gopis;
the melodies of ragas and raginis46 enchant Krishna's heart.

271All the gopis, taking instruments in their hands,
sit and beat the rhythm: "ta thai, ta thai!"

272In the middle both — Radha and Krishna — dance beautifully;
[the gopis] beat the time well: "tati na, tati na!"47

273So the youth and the maiden dance,
with so many playful poses, gazing at each other.

274The movements of their hands go "jhan-jhan",
and with them the sweet sound of bracelets.

275At the swaying of the hips the belt of bells rings in time,
on the feet the anklets ring — sweet to hear.

276Now Krishna makes his beloved Rai48 dance,
and Rai dances with so many movements of her limbs.

277With the movements of their hands the bodice49 of both grew loose;
seeing this, Krishnachandra felt great happiness.

278What happiness it was to see the lotuses of her breasts!
Krishna sank into an ocean of happiness.

279Possessed by the rapture of the dance, he is aware of nothing
and, floating in the sweetness of joy, gazes [at her].

280Now Rai plays the instrument and Hari dances,
and Kishori beats the time: "tadhik, tadhik!"

281Dancing and acting, Krishna, as much as his heart desired,
took his pleasure, sporting with his beloveds.

282To one he gives a smile, another he kisses,
another he embraces, another he draws to his breast.

[p. 88]

283Thus Krishnachandra was immersed in the sweetness of the rasa,
enjoying again and again with the host of his beloveds.

284The gopis embrace Krishna,
and so their hearts are immersed in the sweetness of Krishna's company.

285Thus, in joyful sport, in the sweetness of the rasa,
playing and playing, they reached the end of the night.

286Seeing the night ending, Krishna became as if afraid;
when Krishna vanished from sight, Prabhu returned to outward consciousness.

287"What happened, what happened?" crying, Prabhu rose up.
"I have been robbed of the sight of such happiness!

288Where is Krishna, where is Krishna, the son of Sri Nanda?
Where is Radha, where is Radha's younger sister50, where are the gopis?"

289Not seeing Prabhu, everyone became worried:
"Where has Virachandra gone?" — and they began to search for him.

290Prabhu is not in his bed, the room is empty;
"Where has Prabhu gone?" — everyone was bewildered.

291They looked from temple to temple
and wandered along the banks of the Yamuna searching for him.

292Coming to Dhira-samira and the sandbank of Vamshivata51,
they found Prabhu lying [on the ground].

293From rubbing his face [against the ground] blood was streaming;
seeing him in that state, everyone was distraught.

294In haste they all took hold of Prabhu to lift him,
but they cannot even move Prabhu — Vishvambhara Raya52.

295Then all the devotees, at the top of their voices,
with full throats, began to cry: "Krishna, Krishna!"

296The sound of Krishna's name entered Prabhu's ears;
saying "Krishna, Krishna," Prabhu returned to outward consciousness.

297Looking around, Prabhu saw that four dandas53 of the day [had passed];
restraining his mood, Prabhu went to bathe.

298Having bathed in the Yamuna, he came to the lodging
and, having performed his daily rites, took prasada.

299After rinsing his mouth (achamana)54, Prabhu rested,
saying: "Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna… Rama, Rama."

300The Vaishnavas with him took mahaprasada
and, saying "Govinda, Gauranga!", calmed down a little.

301A dear servant came and massaged Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu, remembering Krishna's pastimes, fell asleep.

302Having stayed thus in Vrindavana for some days,
Prabhu set out for Radhakunda, crying "Gauranga!"

303Behind him hurried all the Vaishnavas with him;
crying "Ha, Krishna Chaitanya!", Prabhu went on.

304Prabhu entered the forest of Bahula55;
coming to the bank of the pond, Prabhu began to weep.

305This is the place of the pastimes of Krishna and Baladeva,
their wonderful pastimes of herding cows with their friends.

306The story of the cow Bahula cannot be told:
she was dear to Rama and Krishna, equal to a wish-fulfilling cow.

307Remembering those pastimes, Prabhu hurried on
and in a moment arrived at Shyamakunda.

308Where Mahaprabhu came and sat beneath a tamala tree,
there at the root of that tamala Prabhu came and sat.

309Crying "Sri Krishna Chaitanya!", he gives a thunderous roar
and says again and again: "This is Prabhu's beloved place!"

310Seeing the waves of Shyamakunda and the radiance of the tamala,
he fainted and fell there.

311The Vaishnavas with him came up
and, arriving, saw Prabhu lying [unconscious].

312Surrounding Prabhu, they sing the sankirtana of Krishna's name,
and that sound entered Prabhu's ears.

313Hearing the sound of Krishna's name, Prabhu returned to outward consciousness
and, with a thunderous roar, cried: "Krishna, Krishna!"

[p. 89]

314Rising, he dances, filled with prema,
crying: "Ha, Krishna Chaitanya, Nityananda!"

315Thus he danced and sang joyfully,
and then rested a while with the devotees.

316What bliss there was when he saw Radhakunda and Shyamakunda —
that I cannot describe.

317Then Prabhu, having circled [the ponds] five or seven times,
came with the devotees to the bank of Radhakunda.

318Where Sri Jahnava had come and rested,
to that very place Prabhu came.

319Above that ghat56 stands one tamala tree:
with great radiance that tree glitters and shimmers.

320There are beautiful steps with a platform set with divine jewels;
how many pastimes Kishori and Kishora performed there!

321Having sported with Radha in the waters of Radhakunda,
[Krishna] sat beneath the tamala with laughter, talk and jest.

322Beautiful Lalita dressed and adorned Krishna,
and Ananga Manjari57 dressed and adorned Rai.

323Looking at Krishna's face, Rai gave a sign,
and the King of rasa understood that sign in his heart.

324Sri Hari himself seized Ananga Manjari, drew her to him
and seated her on his lap.

325"No, no!" saying, the beauty held Krishna off;
then Lalita came and held Radha's younger sister.

326Krishna said: "Dear one, why are you so bashful?" —
and, laughing, Sri Hari himself began to dress her.

327Having dressed and adorned her, Krishna, in waves of bliss,
gazes his fill with both eyes at the beauty of Radha's younger sister.

328What sweet beauty in the lotus face of Radha's younger sister!
The heart of Krishna, enchanter of the world, was filled with longing.

329Enchanted, Krishna could not restrain himself
and held Radha's younger sister in a tight embrace.

330Bringing his face to her lotus face, he kissed her,
and at this the beauty was greatly embarrassed.

331Freeing herself from [his] creeper-like arms and scolding Krishna,
she knit her brows and shot at him the arrow of a sidelong glance.

332Seeing that look, Krishna came over to Rai:
"Look, Radha, your sister is scolding me!"

333Rai laughed and said: "Shameless one, what more is there to say?
What luck for you, to get the touch of Ananga!"58

334So many such pastimes with his beloveds
did Krishnachandra perform, so many sports of rasa!

335Remembering all these pastimes, Virachandra Raya
rolls on the ground beneath the tamala tree.

336"Ha, ha, Radha-Krishna!" he cries with a thunderous roar.
"Ha, ha, Radha's younger sister, my life and soul!

337Ha, ha, Jahnava, my Prabhu, treasure of my life!"59
Saying this, Virachandra weeps.

338At the root of the tamala tree he rolls on the ground
and weeps, crying: "Sri Jahnava, Sri Jahnava!

339Ha, ha, Prabhu Nityananda! Ha, ha, Gaurahari!
Prabhu, accept this lowly one and make him your own."

340Thus Prabhu Virachandra, at Sri Jahnava's ghat,
weeps loudly on the bank of the holy kunda.

341Like golden radiance rolling in the dust,
crying "Ha, ha, Radha-Krishna!", he laments: "Alas, alas!"

342Thus he lamented for some time,
and then, bathing in Radhakunda, he calmed his heart.

343Together with the devotees he ate and rested;
for three days Prabhu stayed there, intoxicated with prema.

344Rising at dawn and bathing at "Manasa Ghata",
Prabhu saw Pancha Pandava60 and set out.

[p. 90]

345Prabhu was agitated with prema, his mind found no rest;
he went on, crying: "Ha, ha, Govardhana Hill!"

346Behind him followed all the Vaishnavas;
Prabhu arrived at "Kusuma Sarovara"61.

347He sat at the root of a keli-kadamba62;
seeing the lake, Prabhu's prema surged up.

348"Ha, ha, Uddhava!" he cries aloud.
"Where is the lord of my life, Krishna, the prince of Vraja?"

349At that time all the Vaishnavas came up;
seeing his companions, Prabhu rose and went on.

350With the gait of a lordly elephant he walked, remembering "Krishna, Krishna,"
and arrived at Govardhana Hill.

351Possessed by the mood of the gopis, with restless mind,
he saw in his heart the pastimes of separation from Krishna:

352"Ha, Krishna, ha, lord of my life, son of the king of Vraja!
Show yourself just once and keep me alive!"

353Seeing Govardhana Hill, he felt Krishna's presence
and, saying "Here is Krishna!", touched the best of hills.

354Touching the best of hills, he took it as touching Krishna.
Such bliss came over him that he was wholly unaware of his body.

355The Vaishnavas with him came up
and all together began to sing the name of Krishna.

356Regaining outward consciousness, Mahaprabhu, crying "Krishna, Krishna!",
went swiftly on, like an enraged lion.

357He came to where Dana-ghati63 is —
where the gopis together paid the toll.

358Remembering all those pastimes,
Prabhu, filled with prema, lost consciousness.

359Fainted from prema, Prabhu lay there;
once again the devotees came up

360and see: Prabhu is lying there without breath.
Seeing this, the devotees nearly gave up their lives.

361The devotees sang of the Danakhanda pastime,
and, hearing it, Virachandra Mahaprabhu returned to outward consciousness.

362He saw [all] the forests of Vrindavana, forest after forest —
the life of Jahnava, his mind agitated with prema.

363I describe the deeds of Prabhu,
singing as best I can, to become purified.

364These qualities and pastimes are the object of the devotees' worship:
whoever honors and remembers them attains Prabhu's feet.

365I have no learning, no ability, no refinement;
I know neither shlokas nor meters — I write in payar.

366I, a man without understanding, pull [the lines] together somehow;
whether what I write is good or bad, I know nothing.

367Knowing me a fool, [Prabhu] out of his own goodness showed me mercy —
that is why he bears the name "Purifier of the fallen."

368He delivered fallen and lowly people;
I see no other such treasury of compassion.

369My wealth, my life is Prabhu Gaurachandra;
his second body is Rama Nityananda;

370his second body is Prabhu Virachandra,
who destroys the darkness in the hearts of living beings, surpassing the full moon.

371He is a body non-different from Gauranga, never other;
have no doubt about this — in him there is no duality.

372In the form of Virachandra, Prabhu descended again:
truly, truly, it was the son of Shachi.

373Nityananda and Virachandra are my life;
birth after birth may my mind remain at their feet.

374Without Gaurachandra, Nityananda and Virachandra,
even if I attain Vaikuntha in my own body, I have no taste for it.

375At the feet of the Vaishnavas I have this one hope:
birth after birth to be a servant of Nityananda.

[p. 91]

376All of you, be merciful to me and fulfill my heart's desire:
birth after birth, be my Lord, Balarama!

377Balarama Nityananda, show me this mercy:
graciously give me the shade of Gaurachandra's feet.

378Placing hope in the feet of Prabhu Virachandra,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the "Vamsha-vistara."

Thus ends the tenth chapter, named "The Journey to Vrindavana," in the Antya-lila of the book "Nityananda-vamsha-vistara" of Sri Nityananda Prabhu.

Translator's Notes

Notes

  1. "Tathahi — padam": a song (pada) in tripadi meter is inserted into the poem — the refrain "Hari, Hari! Will I ever have such a birth again?" and three stanzas. The last word of stanza 5 is corrupt in both copies ("gāu"/"hāi"); by rhyme and sense it is restored as "cāi" ("I want").
  2. Rarh (Radha-desha) — the region west of the Ganga in Bengal (Birbhum, Bardhaman, Bankura), where Virachandra's travels in the previous chapter took place.
  3. Ramai (Ramai Pandita) and Sundarananda — associates of Nityananda and his family.
  4. Jharikhanda — the forested hill country (modern Jharkhand, the Chota Nagpur plateau); by tradition Chaitanya also went to Vrindavana by this route (cf. couplet 64).
  5. Rasavati — "she who is full of rasa," i.e. Radha. Couplets 19–23 set out the teaching of Gauranga as Krishna who has taken on Radha's luster and emotion.
  6. "Srimati" usually means Radha; perhaps the Radha Deity beside Madanamohana is meant.
  7. The tradition about Abhirama: at his obeisances "false" deities would crack, while here Madanamohana merely bent further. In the second line of couplet 25 the corrupt "suvaṅga/suraṅga" is taken as "bent" (rhyming with "vaṅka").
  8. Here "Prabhu" is Nityananda (Balarama), as is clear from couplet 36. "Avadhutashrama" is understood as the period of his wanderings as an avadhuta.
  9. Kanai — an affectionate name of Krishna.
  10. Bali — Balarama.
  11. Both copies have "vaka hao" ("be bent"); from the sense of the next couplet (a height of four of one's own cubits is a sign of a mahapurusha) it is restored as "vaṛa hao" — "grow big."
  12. Jahnavi — the Ganga.
  13. Uddharana Datta — Nityananda's companion on his pilgrimages.
  14. The word rendered "by the same route" is corrupt in the copies ("ebhaḍāija"/"ebhāila"); the translation is conjectural.
  15. Vishnupada — the footprint of Vishnu, the chief shrine of Gaya.
  16. Kashi — Varanasi; Vishveshvara — the Shiva linga, the presiding Deity of Kashi.
  17. "Snana-pana" — literally "bathing and drinking."
  18. Copy A has "bha:ṅgabha bholānātha", restored as "bhāṅgaṛa bholānātha" — "the bhang-intoxicated, simple-hearted Bholanatha," a common epithet of Shiva. For the tale of the king of Kashi and Shiva cf. Bhagavata Purana 10.66 and Chaitanya-bhagavata, Antya-khanda, ch. 2.
  19. The sense of the line "āpanāra śūla rākhe āpane gosāñi" is unclear; the translation is conjectural.
  20. A pun: Bholanatha — "the simple, forgetful lord"; "bhola" — "forgetful."
  21. Ekamra-kanana ("mango grove") — the ancient name of Bhubaneswar in Orissa, a city of many Shiva temples (Lingaraja and others).
  22. Purushottama-kshetra — Puri, the abode of Jagannatha; below, "the place that bears my own name" (couplet 131) is likewise Purushottama.
  23. Yojana — a measure of distance, about 12–13 km.
  24. Havishya — simple purificatory food permitted during vows.
  25. Prayaga — Allahabad (Prayagraj), the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna; Venimadhava — the Vishnu Deity of Prayaga.
  26. Vraja-mandala is traditionally 84 kroshas in circumference; a krosha is about 3 km.
  27. Vrinda Devi — the goddess of Vrindavana, arranger of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.
  28. Ananga — "the bodiless one," Kamadeva; here an epithet of Krishna as Madanamohana. It may also be read as "Radha and Ananga (Manjari)," cf. couplet 322 ff.
  29. "Gaudeshvara Gosai" — it is unclear who is meant: perhaps the head of the Gaudiya Gosvamis of Vrindavana, or a Deity; the translation is literal.
  30. By tradition Jahnava Devi sent to Vrindavana a Deity of Radha, installed at the left of Gopinatha; "Sri Jahnava" here is apparently that image (or Jahnava herself as perceived by Virachandra). The mention of Gopinatha in couplets 179–180 confirms that the Gopinatha temple is meant; a line about it may have dropped out.
  31. Watch (prahara) — a quarter of the day or night, about 3 hours.
  32. Hari — here Virachandra himself.
  33. "Mukhya Haridasa" — apparently Haridasa Pandita, the chief servant of the Govinda temple in Vrindavana.
  34. A well-known shloka ("mukam karoti vachalam…"), usually ending "paramananda-madhavam"; here "paramanandishvaram."
  35. The shloka is badly corrupted in both copies; restored after the known text ("ambhodhih sthalatam sthalam jaladhitam dhuli-lavah shailatam…", Padyavali). Some words of the third line are illegible in the copies.
  36. A pun: "jiva" is both the name of Jiva Gosvami and "living being": he taught both Jiva and the living beings.
  37. Gosaidasa — a pujari, apparently of the Govinda temple.
  38. The text has "piñchana" (literally "peacock feather"), apparently a peacock-feather fan; the reading is not entirely clear.
  39. Thakura — the temple Deity.
  40. "Devalaya" — literally "temple," here the temple people.
  41. Amli-tala (Imli-tala) — a tamarind tree by the Yamuna in Vrindavana where, by tradition, Chaitanya sat.
  42. Shringara-vata — a place in Vrindavana where, by tradition, Krishna adorned Radha; associated with Nityananda.
  43. Gopeshvara — Shiva, guardian of Vrindavana; Vamshivata — the banyan by the Yamuna where Krishna played the flute.
  44. "Radha-Gopinatha, treasure of Jahnava's life" — the Gopinatha Deities of Vrindavana, especially revered by Jahnava.
  45. Pulina — the sandy bank of the Yamuna, the site of the rasa dance.
  46. Ragas and raginis — the male and female melodic modes of Indian music.
  47. "Ta thai," "tati na," "tadhik" — onomatopoeic rhythm syllables (bols).
  48. Rai — Radha.
  49. The copies have "kañca", restored as "kā~cali" — bodice.
  50. "Radha's younger sister" (Radhanuja) — Ananga Manjari, see couplet 322 ff.
  51. Dhira-samira — a place by the Yamuna in Vrindavana; Vamshivata — see note 43.
  52. Vishvambhara — "sustainer of the universe"; a pun: he cannot be lifted. It is also a name of Chaitanya.
  53. Danda — about 24 minutes.
  54. Achamana — ritual rinsing of the mouth after eating.
  55. Bahulavana — one of the twelve forests of Vraja, connected with the tale of the cow Bahula.
  56. Ghat — steps leading down to the water. Here, a ghat on Radhakunda associated with Jahnava (cf. couplet 340).
  57. Ananga Manjari — Radha's younger sister; in the Gaudiya tradition Jahnava Devi is considered her incarnation.
  58. A pun: "Ananga" is both Ananga Manjari and the love-god Kamadeva.
  59. Jahnava is here identified with Ananga Manjari: Virachandra weeps for her, remembering this pastime.
  60. Manasa Ghata (Manasa-ganga?) and Pancha Pandava — places near Govardhana and Radhakunda; the exact reading "mānasa ghāṭa" is unclear.
  61. Kusuma Sarovara — a pond near Govardhana where Krishna met Radha; Uddhava is also venerated there.
  62. Keli-kadamba — a kadamba tree associated with Krishna's pastimes.
  63. Dana-ghati — a place at Govardhana where Krishna playfully exacted a "toll" (dana) from the gopis; the Danakhanda pastimes.
